ruleName: Ball in motion accidentally hits ... the opponent in match play
imagePrompt: A teenage girl golfer on the fairway, having just played a shot that accidentally struck her match play opponent. The players are looking at where the ball came to rest.
imageAlt: Teen girl golfer's ball hits her opponent on the fairway during match play.

issues: Both players are present and appear focused on the ball's position, but the golfer is in address posture rather than post-shot, which slightly reduces narrative clarity.
Club, ball, proportions, posture, and scene are all visually believable and accurate for real golf.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Adjust the girl's posture so it is clearer that she has just finished a shot (not addressing the ball), and ensure both players' attention is focused where the struck ball has come to rest on the fairway. Otherwise, all equipment and scene elements are accurate.

questions.title: What if your ball hits your opponent in a match?
questions.question: You are playing match play. You hit the ball, and it accidentally hits your opponent. What do you do now?

choices.text: Only hit again if both balls were on the putting green.
Always hit the shot again, no matter where you are on the course.
Keep playing from where your ball stopped, unless both balls were on the green.
Add a penalty and hit the shot again.

questions.explanation: If you are playing match play and your ball accidentally hits your opponent, just play your ball from where it stopped. But if both balls were on the putting green before you hit, then you need to play the shot again.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The person you are playing against in your match.
A kind of golf game where each hole is like a separate point against your opponent.
The smooth, short grass area around the hole where you use your putter.

questions.teachingTip: Act out the situation on the putting green and off it so players remember what to do in both spots.
likelyMisconceptions: Some might think you always replay the shot when your ball hits someone.
Some might think you must add a penalty, but you usually don't.

questions.title: Ball accidentally hits opponent in match play
questions.question: During match play, if your ball accidentally hits your opponent, what should you do according to the Rules?

choices.text: Replay the stroke only if both balls were on the putting green.
Always replay the shot, wherever you are on the course.
Play the ball as it lies unless both balls were on the green.
Add a penalty stroke and replay the shot.

questions.explanation: In match play, if your ball accidentally hits your opponent, play your ball as it lies except when both balls were on the green before the stroke. Then, you must replay the shot.
